sentences.text: Per: Justice Avanindra Kumar Singh Learned counsel for the appellant does not wish to press I.A.No.4654 of 2025, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
2. Accordingly, I.A.No.4654 of 2025, is dismissed as not pressed.
3. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, this appeal is heard finally.

4. This appeal under Section 415 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 29/08/2024 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act, 2012), Anuppur (M.P.) in SC No.02/2023, whereby the appellant has been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56035 2 CRA-11688-2024 convicted and sentenced as under :-
Conviction U/s Imprisonment Fine amount In lieu of 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act RI for 20 years Rs.5000/- RI for 6 months 363 of IPC RI for 2 years Rs.1000/- RI for 2 months 366(a) of IPC RI for 2 years Rs.2000/- RI for 2 months Mahesh Baiga @ Raj Baiga vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58783470/
1 5.
The case of the prosecution is that on 29/07/2022 at about 11:00 AM, the complainant and his wife went to the field to sow the seeds and his sister was at home.
When they returned home at 06:00 PM, his sister was not at home.
He inquired her in nearby and relatives but could not find her anywhere.
On the same date, the accused Mahesh Baiga of the locality was also not at home.
He suspected that someone had lured and abducted the minor.
Upon an information at Police Station Jaithari, a case bearing Crime No.381/2022 was registered under Section 363 of IPC and investigation was conducted.
During investigation, the victim was recovered on 07/01/2023 from the house of Kaushalya Bai Kol in village Korja Balghar.

Dastiyabi Panchnama was prepared and the statement under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.
was recorded.
Medical Examination of the victim was conducted and the victim was handed over to the Child Welfare Committee.

On the basis of the statement of the victim, Sections 366-A, 376,
376(2)(A), 376(3) of IPC and Sections 3/4 & 5L/6 of POCSO Act were added against the accused.
Spot map was prepared.
Statements of the witnesses were recorded.
Biological samples of accused and victim were collected.
The samples were sent to FSL, Sagar for DNA test.
Evidence related to the age of the victim was collected.

6. After completion of investigation, the charge-sheet under Sections 363, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56035 3 CRA-11688-2024 366-A, 376, 376(2)(N), 376(3) of IPC and Sections 3/4 & 5L/6 of POCSO has been filed before the competent Court.
When charges were framed the appellant denied the charges and sought trial.

After prosecution evidence, in his statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C, the appellant pleaded innocence and denied the prosecution evidence and submitted that he has been falsely implicated in the case.
However, he did not lead any defence evidence.
7. Learned Trial Court convicted the appellant as mentioned above, against which the appeal has been filed on the ground that the victim and accused are the members of Scheduled Tribes.
They are not governed by Hindu Marriage Act.
No crime is proved against the accused.
The victim being a consenting party having love affair between them.
The trial Court has not appreciated that the victim is being major girl and she is in relationship with accused.
The accused has noting to do with the victim.
There is no criminal antecedent against him.

Merely, on bald and vexatious allegations,
he has been falsely implicated in the case.
The material witnesses have been turned hostile and did not supported the case off the prosecution.
Hence, prays for acquittal.
8. On the other hand, Ms. Shweta Yadav, learned Deputy Advocate General supports the impugned judgment and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

9. Considered the arguments of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10.
As per DNA report (Ex.P/34) accused Mahesh and prosecutrix (PW-1) are the biological father and mother of the newly born child.

The next questions would be regarding age of the prosecutrix on the date of incident i.e. on 29/07/2022 and whether the child born to them was as a result of any offence or it was a consensual relationship.
12. As per court's statement of prosecutrix (PW-1) taken on 03/05/2023, her current age of 17 years whereas the incident is of 29/07/2022 i.e. about 10 months prior.
She stated that she was friend with the accused Mahesh.
They had married and had physical relation, therefore she got pregnant.
In cross-examination, she submitted that she knew that the accused was already married.
She also know that a person who has already married cannot marry again but when accused asked to marry her, she did not refuse.
In Para-6 of her cross-examination, she admitted that in November, 2020 neither accused Mahesh took her anywhere nor he did any wrong with her.
In Para-7 of her cross-examination, she admitted that neither accused Mahesh asked to marry nor asked to make physical relation with him.
In Para-10 she further admitted that they are four brothers and three sisters.
Her elder brother is about 30 years of age and sisters and brothers were born at a interval of 1 year each.
She further stated that she does not know the date of birth or age of any brother and sister.

Therefore, on this ground, if on the date of incident, elder brother of the prosecutrix was 30 years of age and assuming that prosecutrix is the youngest of siblings, her age on the date of incident would be around 19 years.
13. Brother of the prosecutrix (PW-2) has stated that prosecutrix is his sister.
She is aged about 17-18 years.
8 months ago she had gone away somewhere.

When she returned she informed that she got pregnant on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56035 5 CRA-11688-2024 account of physical relation with the accused and thereafter she gave birth to a child.
In para-7 of his cross-examination, he stated that it is true that her sister never said anything against accused Mahesh.
In Para-8 he further stated that her current age is of 28 years and they are four brothers and three sisters and each were having age gap of one year.
In Para-10 he stated that he does not know the actual date of birth of the prosecutrix.
Accordingly, as stated above, on this ground also, on the date of incident, prosecutrix would be more that 18 years of age.
14. Sister-in-law of the prosecutrix (PW-3) has been declared hostile by the prosecution.
Father of the prosecutrix (PW-4) has stated that he does not know the age of the prosecutrix.
She had gone away without informing the family members.
Prosecution has declared this witness as hostile.
In cross- examination by the defence, he stated that he did not know about the incident.
Prosecutrix did not tell him anything against the accused.
15. School Teacher (PW-5) has stated that as per Scholar Register (Ex.P/13), the date of birth of the prosecutrix is 02/02/2006.

In cross- examination, she admitted that at the time of admission,
family members of the prosecutrix did not submit any document regarding date of birth of the prosecutrix and the date of birth was recorded just by estimation.
16. Dr. Preeti Kumere (PW-6) who had conducted the medical examination of the prosecutrix, has submitted that there was no injury on the body of the prosecutrix.

Her secondary sexual characters Mahesh Baiga @ Raj Baiga vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58783470/
3 were fully developed.

sentences.text: She was pregnant.
17. Although prosecution has examined 18 witnesses but above mentioned NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:56035 6 CRA-11688-2024 are the main witnesses.
When we analysis the above oral and documentary evidence, we find that age of the prosecutrix was recorded in school just by estimation.
There was no proof regarding the date of birth of the prosecutrix.
Mother of the prosecutrix could not be examined by the prosecution.
Father has turned hostile.

18. On the basis of statement of prosecutrix (PW-1) and her brother (PW- 2), we find that although it is not mentioned that how many brothers and sisters are elder or younger to the prosecutrix but even assuming that the she was the youngest, therefore if her elder brother was about 28 years of age on 03/05/2023 and if incident is of about 10 months ago, then her brother (PW- 2) would be of 27 years of age on the date of incident and if all the children were born at the interval of one year then on the date of incident, the prosecutrix would not be less than 18 years of age.
Accordingly, we hold that the prosecution has failed to prove by legal evidence that on the date of incident i.e. on 29/07/2022 prosecutrix was less than 18 years of age.

19. Looking to the fact that prosecution has failed to prove that on the date of offence the prosecutrix was less than 18 years of age and looking to the other evidence available on record that a child has been born to them and also looking to evidence of Dr. Preeti (PW-6) that there was no injury marks on the body of the prosecutrix and the facts that the prosecutrix had herself stated about the consensual relationship between them in part of her evidence then the benefit of doubt is required to be granted in favour of the appellant.
20.
Accordingly, appeal is allowed.

The impugned judgment dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:56035 7 CRA-11688-2024 29/08/2024 passed by learned trial Court is set aside.
21. Appellant be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
Case property be disposed off in terms of the orders of the learned trial Court.
Record of the learned trial Court be sent back  (VIVEK AGARWAL)
(AVANINDRA K  JUDGE JUD  mc
